intention: A TREE NODE HOLDS ONE CLAIM, NOT EIGHT. A verdict deposits as its PARTS — one node per verdict and per disposition, each with its own honest vector — and the whole verdict is DERIVED BY READ from the parts, never stored twice. This clears ticket the-deposit-rides-the-read (Stone A), whose verdict has stood pending since 2026-07-29 because its single rendering is 11283 chars against a measured ~7400-char embed ceiling.
why:
THE CEILING WAS NEVER THE PROBLEM — IT WAS THE MESSENGER. MEASURED 2026-07-29: A's verdict is 11283 chars as one node (1.5x over), while its largest single part is 2097 and its smallest 1267 — every part fits with 3.5x headroom. So the wall is GRANULARITY, not capacity, and the embed host refusing was Law 3 doing its job: it surfaced a node-shape error. Look at what one vector over 11283 chars of eight distinct claims actually IS — a centroid of eight unrelated things, pointing nowhere in particular. Eight vectors each pointing at one claim is MORE ACCURATE, not merely smaller. The monolith was already the wrong shape before it was too big; truncation would have hidden the finding and split the vector from its content, which is why it was refused rather than trimmed.

AND THE CLOSE MECHANISM ITSELF IS CAPPED. Stone C's verdict came in at 6418 of ~7400 — I got it under the ceiling by writing DELIBERATELY TERSE evidence, by hand, at close. That is an operator compensating for a missing physics, and the next stone over is a coin toss. [[solidify-the-layer-below]]: a problem surfaced in a lower layer (the deposit/embed seam) and future builds are already unconsciously compensating for it, which is how a 'proven' whole quietly stops being proven. Every subsequent stone's close rides this seam, so it is not Stone A's private blocker — it is the close mechanism's blocker, and it goes in front of the queue.
traces_to: Law 1 — the whole is a READ-PROJECTION of its parts, derived not stored; and without this, every future close re-derives the same workaround (an operator hand-trimming prose to fit a ceiling nobody declared)
Law 3 — the ceiling is measured (7403 embedded / 7447 refused; A at 11283; parts 1267-2097), and the retrieval improvement is labelled a HYPOTHESIS until walked
Law 7 — the pending deposit stayed LOUD and standing rather than being trimmed into a coherent-looking lie; a record of truth never collapses an error
Law 8 — truncating to fit would be a hollow pass: a vector describing bytes the node does not hold

the librarian's tenure loop — parts are the unit of REUSE (node_id_for is a content hash), so a recurring disposition shape dedupes into one node with many corroborations; a monolith can never dedupe, every stone's verdict being unique by construction
state: code-seam@v1: THINKME -> [TICKETME] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> LEARNME -> PROVED   (cast 2026-07-29; leaf, so TICKETME is skippable per the class's skippable_summons; chart pending — the entry gate demands a berthed chart chain before BUILDME)
gates: proof gate: teeth beside the code (cairn/chart/proofs/test_chart_verdict.py extends; the deposit door's own teeth in cairn/librarian/proofs/ must all still green), under the tester with the netns seal. THE PARTS RENDERER: one pure function yields [(kind, content), ...] from the artifact and REMAINS THE SINGLE SOURCE for both what is embedded and what is deposited (the 'one rendering, no drift' why, held per node). THE BOUND IS TOKENS, NOT CHARS: the pre-flight asks the host for prompt_eval_count rather than guessing from length — my 7400-char check was expedient, not correct (chars-per-token swings with punctuation-dense prose). A part over the token bound REFUSES LOUDLY and stands pending, exactly as the monolith did; it is never split further silently. THE COUNT CHECK IS THE PHYSICS: a composition read that recovers fewer parts than the berth declares REFUSES rather than returning a short verdict — this is what makes provenance-append a sibling instead of a prerequisite (see dependencies). LIVE GATE: Stone A's standing pending verdict drains and lands as parts on the first door read — which is a live fire ALREADY WAITING ON THE LEDGER, not one this stone has to manufacture, and it re-opens A's own path from LEARNME to an honest PROVED. Then the NEXT close authored through the new shape, whichever stone that is, must need no operator hand-trimming to fit.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) any part is deposited whose content is not byte-identical to what was embedded for it (the drift this stone must not introduce while fixing granularity); (2) a composition read returns a verdict SHORT of the parts its berth declares, silently — it must refuse (a quietly-short verdict is strictly worse than the loud pending line we have today); (3) a part over the bound is split, summarised, or truncated to fit rather than refused; (4) the whole is persisted anywhere as well as its parts (a second record of truth); (5) an existing monolith node is rewritten or deleted to 'migrate' it — history is append-only and the tree is allowed to be mixed-granularity; (6) the bound is still asked of a character count rather than the host's token count. KILL CONDITION (a3, honest): if constrain finds NOTHING reads the reassembled whole, the composition half is speculative and this stone shrinks to parts-only — that is a win, not a failure of the cast.
horizon: re-read when: the tenure loop lands (parts become corroborated nodes and provenance-append retires the count-check's refusal path); a walk is measured over the split tree (a1 stops being a hypothesis and becomes a number, either way); a second artifact class wants the same treatment (the stage packets deposit as monoliths today and merely HAPPEN to fit — 6418 of 7400 on C is the warning); the embed model changes and the token bound moves.

cairn/chart/live.py deposit_verdict + drain_pending — today `deposit_verdict(artifact, embed(verdict_node_content(artifact)))` is ONE embed of the WHOLE; becomes one embed per part
cairn/librarian/trees.py deposit() — NEEDS NO CHANGE, measured: it takes the vector as a PARAMETER, hashes content for identity, and dim-checks per tree. The ceiling was never in the deposit door

the pending ledger (cairn/chart/verdict.py mark_deposited) — `mark_deposited(berth, node_id)` goes PLURAL (node_ids). THE RECORD-OF-TRUTH RULING, so this does not create two truths: the NODES' provenance is the record of truth (it travels with the data, in the db); the LEDGER is the CROSSING'S RECEIPT (what this crossing discharged). Composition reads provenance; the ledger is how the crossing is audited

SIBLING, NOT PREREQUISITE — provenance-append on a duplicate deposit (trees.py:160 filed edge (b), 'the incoming provenance is dropped for now'). MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: a part that dedupes keeps only the FIRST berth's provenance, so composition-by-provenance would silently miss it. That WOULD be a hard prerequisite except that the count check above makes the hole LOUD instead of silent, and at n=1 A's eight parts are unique prose that will not dedupe. So it is a sibling that retires a refusal path rather than a blocker in front of THE thing. Do not gold-plate this stone by absorbing it; do not ship without the count check either
inference_domain — owns the ceiling contract and already refuses loudly and correctly; this stone asks it for a TOKEN count, it does not re-derive a bound

PATTERN PRECEDENT, NOT A GRAFT (Law 8's distinction, ratified by Akien 2026-07-29: 'precompiled patterns are a win if somebody's doing it RIGHT'): the idea is borrowed, no bytes crossed. Content-addressed parts + composition-on-read is git's object model and CAS generally; per-part embedding over whole-document embedding is settled practice in every retrieval system that works. Cited here as provenance; nothing is vendored, so no graft ticket is owed
provenance: Cast 2026-07-29 through /sorted, at the end of a design arc Akien opened with 'many web servers handle dynamic pages. what would it take to do that here? and if we did, should we also build a separate compositor device?' — the analogy was the whole insight: a dynamic page is COMPOSED AT REQUEST TIME FROM PARTS THE SERVER DOES NOT OWN, which is the shape the tree was missing. THE COMPOSITOR DEVICE WAS DECLINED, on Cairn's own rules and not on preference: two composers with different consumers is premature abstraction (nothing-rides-loose's horizon states the second-proves / third-earns rule), and Law 6 points the other way — every projection in Cairn is owned by the owner of the data it projects (projector for state, pending() for the ledger, render.py for pages), so a compositor device would take composition AWAY from the data's owner and add a hop while owning nothing. A thing that owns no state and produces no data is a FUNCTION, not a device. Seeded by A being back-edged off a falsified PROVED at 6d3ea5b ('the loop fires in anger and finds a ceiling').
